data.continue_conversation: Enable conversations and listen to responses (Experimental)

data_description.model: Which Mistral model to use. Ministral-8b is recommended for home automation commands: fast, cost-effective and great at instruction-following. Ministral-14b is new (Dec 2025) and the strongest of the small edge models. Note: on a free/Experiment-tier API key, the pricier models (Medium, Large) are the ones most likely to be rate-limited or rejected — see the note next to each model below.
data_description.prompt: Instructions for the AI. Supports Jinja2 templates — for example, the HA instance name via ha_name, or the current date via now(). See the README for the full list of variables.
data_description.llm_hass_api: Select which Home Assistant APIs the AI can use. 'Device control' (Assist) controls the entities you expose to voice assistants. 'Home Assistant' lets the AI manage Home Assistant itself (registries, logs, automations) and is admin-only: it is only offered when an admin user is chatting. Voice satellites, automations and other users get the other selected APIs.
data_description.max_tokens: Maximum length of the AI response in tokens.
data_description.reasoning_effort: How much Mistral's reasoning models (such as Mistral Large 4, Medium 3.5 and Small 4) think before they answer. Lower is faster; higher can help with hard questions but adds seconds to every reply, including voice replies and web searches. Mistral Large 4 accepts Low, Medium and High; Medium 3.5 and Small 4 accept None and High. If the model doesn't accept the chosen level (or doesn't reason at all), it is left out for that model and a warning is logged. Also used for web searches, connector requests and AI tasks. 'Default' sends nothing, so Mistral's default applies. The reasoning itself is never spoken; it shows separately in the Assist debug view.
data_description.continue_conversation: When enabled, the assistant automatically keeps listening after a response that ends with a question. Uses the native HA continue_conversation flag. Experimental: behaviour may vary by satellite.
data_description.web_search: When enabled, the AI can search the web for up-to-date information. Uses Mistral's Agents API (beta). Requires a model that supports agents (mistral-small-latest, mistral-medium-latest or mistral-large-latest). See 'Web search routing' below — the 'Always search' option sends every request through the slower Agents API and disables device control for those turns.
data_description.web_search_mode: 'Let the model decide' (recommended): the AI searches only when it decides it needs to, and can still control your devices in the same turn. 'Always search': every request goes through the Agents API — slower, and device control does not work on those turns.
data_description.web_search_trigger: Optional. Comma-separated phrases, for example 'search for, look up, google'. When set, these take precedence over the routing mode: only commands starting with one of these phrases search the web (the phrase itself is removed from the query), and all other commands never search. Leave empty to let the routing mode decide.
data_description.mistral_connectors: Offers every connector (MCP server) registered in your Mistral account to the assistant, so a request such as 'what's on my calendar today' can use it. Mistral runs the connector; results are treated as untrusted and device control is paused for the rest of that turn. Connectors that are not connected or are blocked are skipped. Your API key needs the 'Private and shared connectors' scope to see private connectors. Connectors can take actions (for example send a message), so only connect services you are happy to use by voice. The list is refreshed every 10 minutes. AI-generated content might include information from your connectors, such as Google Maps. When an answer was based on sources, they are listed with links in the 'Mistral AI — connector sources' notification, after a verbatim copy of the question and reply.
data_description.stt_model: Voxtral model used to transcribe speech. The list shows the Voxtral speech models on your Mistral account; you can also type any model ID. Default: voxtral-mini-latest, which always points to Mistral's current transcription model. If speech recognition stops working after a change, check the log and switch back to the default.
data_description.tts_model: Voxtral model used to generate speech. The list shows the text-to-speech models on your Mistral account; you can also type any model ID. Default: voxtral-mini-tts-latest, which always points to Mistral's current text-to-speech model. If speech output stops working after a change, check the log and switch back to the default.
data_description.stt_language: Language for Voxtral speech-to-text. Select 'Auto-detect' to let Voxtral determine the language automatically.
data_description.tts_voice: Fallback voice, used when no voice is chosen under Settings → Voice Assistants and when tts.speak is called without a voice. Type to search by name, slug (for example en_paul_neutral) or 'custom voice': the list holds Mistral's preset voices and the custom (cloned) voices on your account, which are listed first. You can also type a voice ID.
data_description.tts_pace: How fast the voice speaks. Mistral has no speed setting; this is sent as a [pace=…] tag in front of the text, which is not spoken. Only sent when the Text-to-speech model is Voxtral TTS 3 or later (for example voxtral-mini-tts-3-0): voxtral-mini-tts-latest and older models read the tag aloud, so with them it is left out and a warning is logged. Used for Voice Assistant replies and tts.speak (which can override it with the option 'pace'). 'Default' sends nothing.
data_description.tts_emotion: Tone of voice, sent as an [emotion=…] tag. Like the pace, only sent with a Voxtral TTS 3 model (for example voxtral-mini-tts-3-0). Works with Voxtral 3 voices (such as voice_478 and new custom voices); older preset voices such as en_paul_angry have the emotion built into the voice. tts.speak can override it with the option 'emotion'. 'Default' sends nothing.
data_description.tts_expressiveness: From 1.0 to 5.0. Higher values give a stronger delivery but sound less like the chosen voice and less stable. Leave empty to use Mistral's default. tts.speak can override it with the option 'expressiveness'.
data_description.tts_gain_db: Makes the spoken replies louder, in dB. Mistral has no volume setting, so Home Assistant raises the volume of the audio itself; loud parts are rounded off instead of clipping. 0 leaves the audio unchanged. +3 to +6 dB is usually enough; higher values make loud parts sound squashed. tts.speak can override it with the option 'volume_boost'.
data_description.tts_mode: Stream: low-latency SSE WAV with sentence-level pipelining. Batch: single mp3 request, higher latency but smaller responses cache well. The tts.speak service always uses batch.

options.ministral-3b-latest: Ministral 3B — fastest & cheapest, simple commands (free-tier friendly)
options.ministral-14b-latest: Ministral 14B — new, strongest small model (free-tier friendly)
options.mistral-small-latest: Mistral Small — balanced speed & quality (free-tier friendly)
options.mistral-medium-latest: Mistral Medium — needed for web search; ⚠️ paid tier, often rate-limited on free API keys
options.mistral-large-latest: Mistral Large — most capable; ⚠️ paid tier, often rate-limited on free API keys
